The full primary study reports loss of detectable product without MgCl2 or with EDTA, and inactive D14A mutants of both SaPcrB and BsPcrB. Together with the curated cofactor assignment this supports catalytic magnesium binding; the proposed D14 coordination mechanism is distinguished from direct Mg occupancy in the target structure.

PMID:23322418 full text reports SaPcrB structures, wild-type and site-directed-mutant product assays across C20-C40 donors, and chain-length effects. PDBe identifies A7X435 in 3W01/3W02, matching the Mu3 source record. PEG and sulfate in those structures map pocket geometry; they are not a bound natural C35 product. C35 is the supported PcrB reaction, without claiming absolute donor exclusivity or a measured native Mu3 product distribution. The broad term is correct but less informative than the existing specific synthase term; refine to that supported descendant rather than duplicate or discard the claim.

GO:0000107 catalyzes the histidine-biosynthetic phosphoribulosylformimino-AICAR-P/glutamine reaction, not transfer of geranylgeranyl to glycerol phosphate. The target has experimentally curated GGGPS chemistry, bound glycerol-phosphate structure4JEJ, and donor-length mutagenesis. Propagating the broad PTHR21235 HisF-family label through PTN001846602 onto this specialized GGGPS subfamily is biologically inappropriate. This is rejection of a mechanistically conflicting electronic transfer, not an inference from missing literature or a claim of a negative HisF assay.

The curated HAMAP cofactor assignment and conserved Mg-binding features support magnesium as the catalytic metal. This is a mechanistic family inference, not a claim that magnesium occupancy was directly measured in this target crystal. The full 2014 study reports no magnesium density in the groupII structures and treats its position as modeled; the accepted binding function rests on catalytic-family inference, not crystal occupancy.

The InterPro propagation assigns cytoplasm, and the soluble TIM-barrel enzyme is compatible with that location. However, neither the accessible primary abstract nor the curated target record provides a direct cellular localization or an independent target-specific localization inference. Purified recombinant structure is not a cellular localization assay; retain uncertainty rather than inventing a cytosol claim.

The target-specific curated experimental record attributes the C20 reaction and Ile90 mutagenesis to PMID:24684232 and maps to PDB4JEJ. Its group II GGGPS function differs from bacterial group I C35 PcrB. The I90A mutant accepting HepPP is altered specificity and must not be transferred to the wild-type protein. The publisher full text confirms in Figure5 that I90A, unlike wild type, accepts HepPP, and Figure2 uses a B.subtilis delta-pcrB assay host. The frozen cache remains abstract-only, while the separately cited source-scope note records the full-text check.
